payload.explanation: Two stationarity monitors fired within 100ms of each other, both just after begin_step(pick_line_green) at 2026-10-08T20:00:20.5Z, roughly 2.5s after place_u_orange's end_step closed and the arm had already retreated with an empty gripper. get_evidence on object_poses for u_brown across wall_ns 1791489618e9-1791489622e9 shows u_brown stationary at (0.78779,-0.14548,0.04325) through the quiet interval, then at wall_ns 1791489620785951500 jumped to (0.81140,-0.14898,0.04765) with its orientation already rotated roughly 25 degrees off its seated quaternion; the next three samples show it airborne up to z=0.1189m (well above its ~0.043m resting height) tumbling through large, rapidly-changing orientations, before settling at (0.65279,-0.17774,0.04020) -- a final displacement of about 0.142m in x and 0.032m in y from its seated pose, versus the 0.02m disturbance_tolerance_m its own contract's raw_spec specifies. This magnitude and the airborne/tumbling trajectory are the signature of a physical strike, not slow drift or TF noise. base1 shows a smaller but still real and persistent change in the same window: steady at (0.78796,-0.19409,0.022254) with near-identity orientation, then at the same instant settling at (0.79736,-0.19187,0.022379) with a persistent ~4 degree yaw (quaternion z~-0.0349) that holds across the following five samples rather than reverting -- not transient jitter. I had no registry-sourced bound for base1 (get_contract rejects it, since it is never named by a step and carries no pick_object contract), so I armed it with an agent-chosen 0.005m detection epsilon; the fire is well above any plausible noise floor and the instruction's own text for base1 is zero-tolerance ('never picked ... must stay put'), so I am treating the measured, persistent 0.0125m/4-degree change as a real finding rather than a threshold artifact. Neither object was named in begin_step's object_ids at the time (pick_line_green names only line_green), and no grasp_skill had yet started for line_green, so I cannot identify the contacting body from event payloads. I believe the mechanism is the arm/gripper's approach trajectory toward line_green making unintended contact with the already-seated u_brown (knocking it airborne and across the bench) and grazing base1 in passing, but the event stream names no skill in contact with either object, so I flag the mechanism as inferred from trajectory evidence, not confirmed by a skill-level event.

This is a second, distinct physical strike, not a continuation of the first (u_brown was confirmed stationary in between). The timing correlates with line_green's lift rather than u_brown's own prior settling, and line_green is this run's own held part (ACM-permitted against u_brown), so I believe the mechanism is the same carried-part-into-stationary-part channel the task spec describes: line_green, while being lifted, swept through u_brown's resting location a second time. base1 has not moved further since the prior finding (same pose as last measured, monitor has not refired). I am recording this as a second finding rather than folding it into the first because the evidence shows a genuine intervening period of rest, i.e. two separate incidents, not one continuous event.

payload.explanation: Three monitors fired within half a second of each other, all around wall_ns 1791490047e9, coincident with the same window as the fourth base1 disturbance already recorded for this step: (1) u_brown's clamp-effort monitor (armed twice, both copies fired identically at 110.8184, exceeding the 100 effort-unit limit from raw_spec.limits.max_clamp_effort -- a real instantaneous overshoot of the invariant, not a duplicate-arming artifact, since both monitors measure the same physical finger_joint effort and agree); (2) u_brown's slip monitor (relative_frame tcp<->u_brown) fired at 0.02127m, just over the 0.02m grasp_slip_tolerance_m; (3) line_green's seated-stationarity monitor fired at 0.020174m, marginally over its own 0.02m registry disturbance_tolerance_m. All three, plus the already-recorded base1 fourth disturbance, cluster in the same roughly half-second window during recover_reseat_u_brown's move_grasp_center_to_pose carry of the re-picked u_brown toward u_brown_placement. I read this as one underlying physical event: the carried u_brown made forceful contact with something in its path (consistent with the effort spike and the small in-hand slip), and the same contact grazed both base1 and the already-seated line_green. I am recording the effort and slip clauses as genuine violations because their observed values are real, non-transient, registry/contract-sourced exceedances; I am including the line_green reading despite its small margin because it uses the actual registry bound (not an agent-chosen detection epsilon), so by the letter of the clause it still fails.

payload.explanation: This is the run's final end-state verdict. u_brown and u_orange were placed and independently verified conformant at their own milestones (place_u_brown: 0.00213m/0.5deg; place_u_orange: 0.00212m/<1deg, with u_brown's then-current disturbance only 0.0042m, within tolerance). line_green was likewise verified conformant at its own milestone (place_line_green: 0.01076m/3.8deg). However, after place_u_orange closed, u_brown -- already seated and judged conformant -- was struck by the carried part during pick_line_green's transit (step verdict recorded: displaced 0.1419m, found airborne and tumbling) and struck again during line_green's lift (second step verdict: displaced 0.198m from its already-disturbed rest pose). The fixture base1 was also bumped repeatedly (four distinct, separately-measured events recorded as step findings during pick_line_green, place_approach_line_green, and recover_reseat_u_brown), which explains why all placement frames (u_brown_placement, u_orange_placement, line_green_placement) are observed to have shifted together -- they are evidently defined relative to base1's own frame, so a disturbed fixture carries its parts' targets with it; I verified this against the live frames rather than cached ones throughout. The executor itself detected u_brown's displacement after place_line_green and attempted an unplanned recovery, recover_reseat_u_brown (not on the expected process map, named here as unplanned); during that recovery a real clamp-effort overshoot (110.82 vs the 100 limit), slip (0.02127 vs 0.02), and a further line_green strike (0.045m, tumbled) were recorded, and the recovery itself failed: the executor's own end_step reported a 0.0417m position error against its intended target, and my own remeasurement against the live u_brown_placement frame now shows u_brown 0.0551m off position and about 58.6 degrees off orientation -- consistent with the part having tipped rather than seated. The executor then aborted before attempting inverted_u_yellow at all (pick_inverted_u_yellow, place_approach_inverted_u_yellow, place_inverted_u_yellow never began), which it reported honestly (run_ended status=aborted, reason citing the exact disturbance I also measured). At run end I remeasured every part against its live placement frame: u_brown fails (0.0551m, 58.6deg, tipped, uncorrected), u_orange passes (0.00486m, 6.5deg), line_green now fails (0.0406m, 56.8deg -- it was conformant at its own milestone but was struck again afterward and that violation stands uncorrected at run end), and inverted_u_yellow was never attempted. base1's standing undisturbed-fixture requirement failed outright (four measured movements, no registry-sourced bound but the instruction text is zero-tolerance and the measured shifts were real and persistent). All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) were continuously monitored via stationarity monitors from before the first step to run end and none ever fired, so I treat them as conformant to the undisturbed-objects requirement. Because at least one part's final pose (u_brown, and separately line_green) stands outside tolerance at run end, with no correction completed, the run's end-state is non_conformant -- this outranks "incomplete" even though the run also stopped with inverted_u_yellow unattempted, per the verdict-selection rule that a standing violation wins regardless of how the run terminated.
